about: Replayable orchd tasks: each starts at the parent of a commit that already solved it; `reference` is that commit, for comparison only. Mixed sizes: mechanical, standard, UI and daemon. Kept small: run it before a flag becomes a default or after a big harness change; day-to-day A/B runs on real backlog requests.

tasks.name: attempt-counter
tasks.request: The orchestrator task detail header shows 'attempt N/M' where N is the daemon's global attempt number across plan, implement and review stages, so a task on its first implementation attempt can read 'attempt 3/4'. Make it count implementation attempts only, in the header and wherever the panel counts attempts toward the limit; cover it in tests/orchestrator-helpers.test.cjs.

tasks.name: unfenced-json
tasks.request: Codex sometimes drops the backticks around its final sushi-report or sushi-review block and sends the bare tag line followed by the JSON; orchd then finds no report or no verdict. Parse that form too, keep fenced blocks working, and add a unit test built from such a reply.

tasks.name: base-branch-field
tasks.request: In the orchestrator panel's '+ New task' form (src/orchestrator/OrchestratorPanel.tsx), add an optional base branch field so a task can start from another branch; it is passed as `base` to task.create (orchd already accepts it) and defaults to the repo's current branch. Show the branch a task started from (task.baseRef) in the task detail header. Prove the form and the header with screenshots saved under artifacts/.

tasks.name: task-costs
tasks.request: orchd task costs are too low: the plan run and the review run report a cost that is never added to the task, and Codex runs report tokens but no cost at all. Add plan and review costs to the task total, price Codex runs from per-model prices kept in settings (with built-in list prices for the Codex models in use), and make `orchd ab` leave out tasks created before variants existed so they don't skew the default arm.
